/-!
# Conjecture 7.3

by S. I. Adian

Prove that the periodic product of odd exponent $n \geq 665$ of non-trivial groups
$F_1, \ldots, F_k$ which do not contain involutions cannot be generated by less than $k$
elements. This would imply, on the basis of (S. I. Adian, *Sov. Math. Doklady* **19** (1978),
910–913), the existence of $k$-generated simple groups which cannot be generated by less than
$k$ elements, for any $k > 0$.

Here the periodic product is Adian's $n$-periodic product (S. I. Adian, *Periodic products of
groups*, Trudy Mat. Inst. Steklov **142** (1976), 3–21), defined by the Novikov–Adian inductive
relator scheme on the free product of the factors. This construction is not available in
Mathlib, so the first sentence is not stated in this file. Only the consequence about simple
groups is formalized.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

For every $k > 0$ there exists a $k$-generated simple group which cannot be generated by less
than $k$ elements: a simple group $G$ with a generating set of $k$ elements such that every
finite generating set of $G$ has at least $k$ elements.

The Kourovka Notebook records this as a consequence of Problem 7.3, via Adian's simplicity
theorem for periodic products (S. I. Adian, *Sov. Math. Doklady* **19** (1978), 910–913).

claims.decomposer_note: Implicit universal quantifiers over k ≥ 1, every odd n ≥ 665 and every family of k nontrivial groups without elements of order 2; 'periodic product' is Adian's n-periodic product (Adian 1976, defined by an inductive relator scheme on the free product; not in Mathlib, must be defined), and 'cannot be generated by less than k elements' means no generating subset of cardinality < k (i.e. rank ≥ k, so together with the obvious k-element generating set from the factors the rank is exactly k).
claims.reviewer_why: Omitted. The statement is about Adian's n-periodic product, defined via the Novikov–Adian inductive elementary-period scheme, which is absent from Mathlib/FormalConjecturesForMathlib. Only two candidates attempted a bespoke definition and neither is verifiably faithful. c05 quotients the free product by the n-th powers of all elements not conjugate into a factor; this is provably a different group (with c = h·g' and g ∈ F_1 of order not dividing n, w = g·cⁿ is cyclically reduced of length ≥ 2, so wⁿ is a relator while cⁿ is too, forcing gⁿ = 1 — the factors do not embed, contradicting Adian's embedding theorem), so its theorem is about the wrong object. c06 gives a rank-by-rank scheme (kill xⁿ for |x| ≤ α+1 not conjugate into a factor modulo the rank-α relations); it compiles and agrees with Adian at small ranks, but its equality with Adian's construction depends on unverified stability results of the Novikov–Adian theory and on the exact definitions in Adian 1976, which c06 itself flags as its 'main point of uncertainty' (confidence 0.7). Six candidates independently bailed with well-argued missing_primitives reasons. Since a wrong bespoke definition would make the theorem about a different group, the slot is omitted rather than shipped.

claims.decomposer_note: Stated consequence of the main claim via Adian's 1978 simplicity theorem for periodic products: for every k > 0 there is a simple group generated by k elements but by no fewer (rank exactly k); it is a subordinate weaker form, and the notebook does not record its independent status, so it could be formalized either as the bare existence Prop or as the implication from the main statement.
claims.reviewer_why: Bare existence form (permitted by the table, and the only option once the main slot is omitted): ∀ k > 0, ∃ simple group G (Mathlib IsSimpleGroup, which includes Nontrivial) with a generating Finset of cardinality exactly k and such that every generating Finset has ≥ k elements. Restricting to Finsets loses nothing (a generating set with < k elements is finite). Equivalent to Group.FG G ∧ Group.rank G = k (c08's form) and to the encard/Cardinal forms of c04/c07; the explicit Finset form (identical in c01, c02, c06, up to binder style in c03) is the most transparent. Docstrings lightly edited.

decomposition_objections.text: The table's note that the periodic product 'must be defined' presupposes that Adian's n-periodic product can be defined in a problem file. Its genuine definition is the full Novikov–Adian inductive scheme (dozens of mutually inductive notions on words of the free product), and no simple intrinsic characterization valid for all odd n ≥ 665 is available (the Adian–Atabekyan characterization requires n ≥ 1003; naive quotient descriptions give a different group). So the main slot is not formalizable without first developing this machinery in FormalConjecturesForMathlib. For the variant slot, the notebook gives no independent status; the table (and the harness) treat it as open, but it may be a known result via other constructions, so its category should be double-checked.

items: The variant slot is formalized as the bare existence statement (∀ k > 0, ∃ simple G of rank exactly k), not as the implication from the main statement, since the notes call it a 'subordinate weaker form' and the main statement could not be stated. It is tagged `research open` to match the recorded status; a reviewer should check whether the existence of simple groups of every finite rank is known independently (e.g. via Olshanskii/Obraztsov-type constructions), in which case `research solved` would be appropriate.

'Cannot be generated by less than k elements' is quantified over finite generating sets (`Finset G`) with `k ≤ S.card`; infinite generating sets are irrelevant to 'less than k elements', and using `Set.ncard` (which is 0 on infinite sets) would have been wrong.

'k-generated' is rendered as the existence of a generating Finset of cardinality exactly k; together with the lower bound this is equivalent to `Group.rank G = k` (Mathlib's `Group.rank` is the least such cardinality), but the explicit form avoids an existentially quantified `Group.FG` instance.
The witnessing group is quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following the convention of other Kourovka files (e.g. 1_74.lean).
The module docstring reproduces the full problem (including the omitted main claim) and states that the n-periodic product is not formalized, so the file is self-describing about its scope.

reviewer_notes: Final file ships only the second slot. Category `research open` follows the harness status; the notebook gives no independent status for this consequence, and its independent truth (simple groups of rank exactly k for every k, e.g. via Ol'shanskii/Obraztsov/Guba-type constructions) may be known in the literature — a human should double-check whether `research solved` is more appropriate. Note the decomposition table's remark that 'together with the obvious k-element generating set the rank is exactly k' holds only when the factors are cyclic; the main slot itself is just the lower bound, and this does not affect the shipped slot. Universe: witness group quantified over `Type`, as in existing Kourovka files. Reference given as arXiv 1401.0300v46 matching the cited source version.
